A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same VCI research work. Their main text, equations, tables, figures, proofs, and appendices are accessible and support reliable comparison after matching reordered sections.

before.justification: V1 reports original experiments on Sciplex, Marson, Morpho-MNIST, and CelebA-HQ, including benchmark comparisons, component ablations, and marginal-estimator results.

after.justification: V2 retains these original experiments and adds a Diff-SCM comparison, latent-consistency and axiomatic diagnostics, and qualitative digit-intervention results.

M1.justification: The VCI objective, encoder-decoder workflow, counterfactual supervision, latent-divergence regularizer, and robust marginal estimator are retained. Architecture and gradient-detaching descriptions also match. Terminology refinements and additional evaluations do not introduce a new method component.

E1.justification: V2 Figure 13 adds digit-identity interventions on Morpho-MNIST, extending the original thickness/intensity intervention tasks. Sciplex, Marson, and CelebA-HQ coverage remains unchanged. This is a limited task extension within an existing dataset.

E2.justification: Diff-SCM becomes an evaluated comparator in v2 Table 2 and its accompanying uncertainty table; v1 discussed it but reported no corresponding benchmark scores. The existing comparator sets are retained. The new diagnostic comparison in Table 7 uses previously evaluated MED and SAE.

E3.justification: V2 adds diagnostic protocols using KL divergence to measure oracle consistency, a latent-divergence coefficient sweep from 0 to 0.05, and composition/effectiveness/reversibility measurements on an L2 scale. Appendix M retains the established benchmark splits, preprocessing, architectures, and training settings.

E4.justification: Beyond the retained component ablations, v2 Appendix N.3 adds direct evaluation of latent consistency across regularization strengths. Appendix N.4 adds empirical axiomatic diagnostics against MED, replacing v1's discussion without corresponding measurements. These substantially expand analysis of the claimed disentanglement mechanism and counterfactual-model behavior.

E5.justification: Both versions report five independent runs, standard errors, and violin plots for the established experiments. V2 extends uncertainty-bearing results to additional comparisons, but documents no changed run counts, seeds, significance tests, or uncertainty-estimation procedures. The new tables do not establish a different statistical reporting practice.

E6.justification: V2 adds substantive result sets: Diff-SCM scores, including mixed image MSE of 6.30 × 10^-2; oracle-consistency KL decreasing from 3979.86 to 0.51 across the coefficient sweep; and Table 7's finding that VCI has better effectiveness and reversibility but worse composition than MED. Figure 13 adds digit-intervention examples. Existing Tables 1 and 5 and the shared Table 2 scores remain unchanged.

T1.justification: V2 corrects the Pinsker bounds in Equations 43 and 72 from KL divergence to the square root of half the KL divergence, and clarifies the zero-divergence reasoning. Appendix F also makes the marginal encoder distributions explicit. The theorem statements and substantive assumptions are retained; collecting existing assumptions into Appendix H is reorganization.

C1.justification: Both versions claim an individual-level counterfactual ELBO, end-to-end supervision without counterfactual observations, treatment-disentangled representations, robust marginal estimation, and benchmark advantages. Replacing 'latent disentanglement' with 'disentangled exogenous noise abduction' clarifies the already stated meaning rather than changing the contribution.

C2.justification: V2 expands the diffusion critique by connecting noise destruction and digit-changing interventions to the consistency assumption. Its revised diagnostic discussion explains why VCI can have nonzero composition error and emphasizes tradeoffs among the three axiomatic metrics. V1 already discussed metric limitations, but lacked this interpretation of measured diagnostic results.

D1.justification: V1 refers readers to a code repository in supplementary material; v2 Appendix M supplies a direct codebase URL. The existing architecture, hyperparameter, hardware, and detaching details are retained. The PDFs establish improved access instructions, without establishing the repository's external availability.

R1.justification: V2 adds Komanduri et al. (2024) on causal diffusion autoencoders and Melistas et al. (2024) on counterfactual-image benchmarking. It removes the Shadow-dataset and UK Biobank references with the shortened metrics discussion and expands its positioning against diffusion approaches. The principal relationship to earlier VAE and adversarial methods remains intact.

P1.justification: V2 makes localized prose and terminology edits, swaps the related-work and VAE-comparison appendices, collects existing causal assumptions into a separate appendix, and replaces the lengthy metrics discussion with a shorter results-linked discussion. It also adds author contributions. Most of the main narrative and technical exposition is retained.

P2.justification: V2 adds Tables 6–7 and Figure 13, expands the benchmark and uncertainty tables with Diff-SCM rows, relocates existing displays, and adopts ICLR headers and typography. Existing figure contents, including the ablation curves and violin plots, are retained. These are localized display additions and layout changes.

improvement.justification: V2 modestly strengthens empirical support through an evaluated diffusion baseline and new mechanism and axiomatic diagnostics, while correcting two proof inequalities and providing clearer code-access instructions. Table 7 usefully exposes a composition-versus-effectiveness/reversibility tradeoff. The core method and established results remain unchanged, and the additions do not establish the broad diffusion-incompatibility arguments in Appendix C.1, limiting the overall gain.
